claims.text: A minor refractory-element addition will enhance the elevated-temperature yield strength of the HEA relative to the same HEA without the addition.
Hafnium is an example of a refractory element suitable for the proposed minor addition.
The refractory-element addition will promote segregation of that element to grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary segregation of the refractory element will lead to thermally stable boundary phases.
Segregation of the refractory element to grain boundaries will reduce grain-boundary diffusion.
Segregation of the refractory element to grain boundaries will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Reduced boundary diffusion and impeded grain-boundary sliding will stabilize the microstructure under high-temperature stress.
The stabilized microstructure will produce a measurable increase in yield strength under application-specific elevated-temperature conditions.
General understanding of grain-boundary engineering in similar alloys supports the proposed qualitative enhancement mechanism.
The exact magnitude of the yield-strength improvement is uncertain.
